findings.quote: | Extra time in English | [ESL +30](../facts/exam.md#exam-esl-accommodation): a [30-minute exam extension](../facts/exam.md#exam-esl-accommodation) for non-native English speakers |
findings.evidence: Fact exam-esl-accommodation in data/facts/exam.jsonl is status 'mech-pass' (rev 2, amended_by requests-00, mech checked 2026-10-12T07:06:28Z, votes empty), not 'verified'. facts/exam.md has no '### exam-esl-accommodation' heading (only line 411 'Replaced by [exam-esl-accommodation]'), so all four links in 1-fast.md (table row, and the trap at line 53) point to a missing anchor. RULINGS 2026-10-09: exam-esl-accommodation is one of the four facts the web shell reads; RULINGS 'Rulings where the planning reports differ': lint fails when the fact is not verified. The amend happened after the prose and edit stages passed, so the ledger did not catch it. Also line 53 'You request ESL +30 one time, before you register for an exam' states the 'once, before registering' part without a link; the fact's display 'requested once, prior to registering for an exam' should carry it. All other 70 linked fact ids in the chapter are verified with anchors present.
findings.resolution: fix-01: exam-esl-accommodation is verified again (entail vote at rev 2) and facts/exam.md has its entry; lint 01 is clean. The trap's Truth now carries the before-registering claim in a sentence linked to the fact ('apply to all future exam registrations'). The display 'requested once, prior to registering for an exam' cannot be used: 'prior to' is a banned word (L801).

findings.quote: - "Create one NAT gateway in a public subnet ...": It works, but the stem accepts an interruption, and three gateways cost more than one because the number of gateways is billed.
findings.evidence: Rule: the reader must be able to tell which option a Why-not line rejects (READER.md: she trusts the gist from one glance). Options in 5-quiz.md carry no letters, and the generator truncates each rejected option to its first words. In questions.json q002 this line is option b ('...in each Availability Zone...'), but the truncation is identical to the start of correct option a ('Create one NAT gateway in a public subnet in one Availability Zone...'), so the answer appears under Why not. The same collision with the correct answer happens in Question 2 (q008: 'Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 ...' is option c; correct b starts the same), Question 7 (q006: 'Create one NAT gateway in a public subnet ...' is option a; correct b starts the same) and Question 10 (q011: 'Create an SCP that denies the deletion of ...' is option c; correct d starts the same). Two distractors share one label in Question 1 (q004: both interface-endpoint options) and Question 9 (q010: 'Add an inbound deny rule for the address ...' twice). Fix in the generator: print option letters (A to E) and refer to them, or truncate at the first word that differs.
findings.resolution: fix-01: same fix as claims-013. Every colliding wrong option (q002 b, q004 b and c, q006 a, q008 c, q010 b and c, q011 c) now starts its why by naming itself, for example 'One gateway in each zone works, but ...'. Stems, option texts and keys are unchanged, so the verification stands. The 8-word handle itself is fixed by TOOLS-items.md 6.2; letters or a unique-prefix handle are a contract change for the orchestrator.

findings.quote: The word **ensure** asks for a control that enforces or prevents, not one that only detects.
findings.evidence: No fact grounds this reading rule, and the exam guide itself uses 'ensure' for goals that are not preventive controls. Fact exam-guide-backup-retention-wording, quote (Content Domain 2): "Implementing strategies to ensure the durability and availability of data (for example, backups)". A backup is a recovery measure, not a control that prevents. The rule repeats as an absolute in the 2-deep.md table row 'ensure | make it certain | a control that enforces or prevents, not one that only detects or reports', in the fast trap "'Ensure' asks for a control that prevents the action, even for the root user", and in the q011 Takeaway 'Ensure plus the root user means prevention by an SCP'. A reader who applies it to a stem such as 'must ensure that the security team is notified' or 'ensure the durability of data' rejects the right answer. Narrow it: ensure makes the requirement hard; when the stem says ensure that an action cannot happen, a detective control alone does not meet it.
findings.resolution: fix-01: narrowed as suggested (same fix as claims-002): ensure makes the requirement hard; 'ensure that no one can delete' asks for prevention; 'ensure the durability of data' can be met by backups. Fast paragraph, trap, exam-English row, Check 2 and q011 why, explanation, takeaway and say changed.

findings.quote: **MOST or LEAST in capitals** tells you that more than one option works.
findings.evidence: Absolute claim without a fact (RULINGS hard rule 1). The verified fact exam-select-best-response-instruction only says to choose what can 'best complete the statement or answer the question'; it does not say that a capital qualifier implies several working options. Repeated in the 2-deep.md and exam-english.md row 'MOST or LEAST in capitals | more than one option works'. If she believes it, a stem where only one option meets the requirements makes her doubt the right answer and look for a second 'working' one. Say 'often more than one option works; the capital word ranks the ones that do'.
findings.resolution: fix-01: 'usually means that more than one option works' in 1-fast; the row meaning (2-deep and exam-english.md, from data/exam-english.json) is 'often more than one option works; rank the options that work'.

findings.section: The nine word groups / Optimisation qualifiers
findings.quote: Four qualifiers repeat the domain names ... So the qualifier also tells you which domain the question tests. MOST secure matters most, because the secure domain is the largest
findings.evidence: Rule: cause and effect must follow (reader lens). The text does not say which four qualifiers it means (the table holds MOST secure, MOST resilient, MOST cost-effective, but no 'MOST high-performing'). The inference 'the qualifier tells you the domain' is unsupported: the chapter's own items show LEAST operational overhead (no domain name) on security questions q003, q007, q010, q011. 'MOST secure matters most because the secure domain is the largest' is a non sequitur: the domain weight (fact exam-domain-weights) says how many questions test security, not that the MOST secure qualifier is more important. Cut the second and third sentence or rewrite as a tendency.
findings.resolution: fix-01: same as claims-004. The inference and the non sequitur are cut; the paragraph names MOST secure, MOST resilient and MOST cost-effective and says the qualifier does not tell the domain.

findings.section: Read the stem in this order
findings.quote: A stem has four parts: context, a problem or change, zero to three constraints, and the ask.
findings.evidence: The number 'zero to three' has no source and the chapter contradicts it: the worked example q004 (5-quiz.md Question 1, think-aloud step 2) marks four constraints ('the uploads go to Amazon S3 in the same Region, they come only from the instances in the VPC, they must reach Amazon S3 privately, and the NAT gateway data processing charge is the cost to cut'); q011 has 'must ensure', 'including the root user', 'centrally manage' plus the qualifier. A reader who counts three and stops misses the fourth. Drop the number ('one or more constraints') or say 'usually two to four' as this book's observation.
findings.resolution: fix-01: the number is dropped: 'In this book, a stem has four parts: context, a problem or change, the constraints, and the ask.'

findings.quote: **Check 2.** Time runs out, and three questions are blank. Should you guess?
findings.evidence: READER.md: 'Headings, tables and captions must give a correct gist on their own; questions must test what the gist misses.' The skim (headings, bold, tables, captions) already gives the answer: bold step 6 '**Answer every question.**' plus the trap bolding. Predict 2 and Recap 3 are also read straight from the skimmed table (acceptable for recap, not for Check). Check 1 is not fully answerable from the skim, which is good. Replace Check 2 with an item the skim misses, for example why an answer that 'works' can still be wrong, or which option survives when the cheapest one misses an 'acceptable' relaxation.
findings.resolution: fix-01: Check 2 now asks whether 'must ensure the durability of its data' removes an option that takes backups; the answer (No) is grounded in exam-guide-backup-retention-wording and is not in the skim. The Predict 2 answer stays in that reveal.

findings.quote: ## The nine word groups (9 min) ... ### Optimisation qualifiers (1 min)
findings.evidence: READER.md: 'Depth lives in short subsections with a time box and a Stop-and-answer'. 2-deep.md has no Stop-and-answer or retrieval prompt anywhere: nine subsections, each one with two paragraphs and a 10-row, 3-column table (90 words), boxed at 1 minute each. For a second-language reader who must learn the words, 1 minute per 10 dense rows is not realistic, and the false time box will push her to skim the tables she is meant to learn. Add one Stop-and-answer per group (for example a twin pair: 'must continue' vs 'acceptable': which answer changes?) and raise the boxes to 2 to 3 minutes.
findings.resolution: fix-01, time boxes done: each group is now 2 minutes, the section 18 minutes, and the full route in the front matter 56 minutes. Not done: a Stop-and-answer per group. The prompt label 'Stop and answer.' is defined only for role how (SPEC prompts.labels; L107 in this method section), and the section is already over its 1,200-word budget (W201). A practice device for the word groups needs an orchestrator decision (a role or label for it).

findings.section: The nine word groups / Strength of requirement
findings.quote: In this book, must means that AWS requires something; in a stem, must states the company's requirement.
findings.evidence: STYLE (one term per concept, plain English) and READER.md (forgets terminology under stress). The sentence gives one word two meanings in the same paragraph that teaches 'must' as the strongest stem word, and the book convention it refers to is not explained here. It adds a load without helping her read a stem. Remove it, or move it to the chapter 00 conventions where the book's own wording rules live.
findings.resolution: fix-01: the sentence is removed.

findings.quote: **Truth:** The guide writes [a highly available and/or fault-tolerant architecture across AWS Regions or Availability Zones](../facts/exam.md#exam-guide-highly-available-fault-tolerant-wording): two requirements. Fault tolerant accepts no interruption.
findings.evidence: The cited quote (fact exam-guide-highly-available-fault-tolerant-wording: "Determining the AWS services required to provide a highly available and/or fault-tolerant architecture across AWS Regions or Availability Zones") does not support 'two requirements' ('and/or' shows overlap) and says nothing about interruption. The definitions 'highly available ... a short interruption is acceptable' and 'fault tolerant ... with no interruption' (1-fast.md core words, 2-deep.md Optimisation qualifiers paragraph and table) carry no fact link. The availability definition the book does have (well-architected-availability-definition, 'percentage of time that a workload is available for use') is not used here. Ground the distinction in a Well-Architected or whitepaper quote, or mark it as the book's working definition.
findings.resolution: fix-01: same as claims-003. No AWS page in the canon defines the difference, so it is marked as the book's reading ('This book reads them as two strengths'), and the trap Truth no longer claims 'two requirements'.

findings.quote: **Terminate** (TER-mih-nayt) or stop: terminate deletes the instance; stop pauses it.
findings.evidence: 'Pause' suggests the instance keeps its state, which is what hibernation does. Fact ec2-state-stopped-not-billed, quote: "| `stopped` | The instance is shut down and cannot be used. The instance can be started at any time. | Not billed |"; fact ec2-state-diff-instance-store-data: instance store data "The data is erased" on stop. Exam questions contrast stop and hibernate, so 'pauses' plants the wrong picture. Write 'stop shuts it down; the EBS volumes stay, and you can start it again'.
findings.resolution: fix-01: 'stop shuts it down, which is not a pause.' The cited ec2-state facts are mech-pass, not verified, so the EBS and start-again detail is not linked or added yet.

findings.quote: A **principal** (PRIN-sih-pul) makes a request; its sound-alike ending in -ple means a rule.
findings.evidence: READER.md: English is her second language. The confusable word 'principle' is never written, so she must build it from 'ending in -ple'. A confusable pair needs both spellings side by side: 'principal (makes a request) or principle (a rule, as in the principle of least privilege)'.
findings.resolution: fix-01: tried and reverted. The lint bans the spelling as a variant of the term principal (L901 banned variant `principle`), so the pair cannot show both spellings. The line keeps 'its sound-alike ending in -ple means a rule'. Changing the term rule is an orchestrator decision.

findings.quote: The security team must ensure that no one in the member accounts, including the root user, can delete the flow logs ... attach the SCP once to the root of the organization in AWS Organizations.
findings.evidence: One item uses 'root' in two meanings (the root user of an account; the root of the organization tree), and the Why repeats both ('the strongest actor in the stem is the root user ... One SCP on the organization root'). 2-deep.md 'Confusable words' lists 'Route or root: ... root is the root user' only, which tells her that root always means the root user. Add the pair 'root user or organization root' to Confusable words.
findings.resolution: fix-01: added 'Root user or organization root: one identity in one account, or the top of AWS Organizations, above all accounts.' and changed the route line to 'root often means the root user'.

findings.quote: This book sorts them into six types, so that you can name the type:
findings.evidence: 2-deep.md Instruction grammar teaches six distractor types 'so that you can name the type', and questions.json stores a distractor_type for every wrong option (for example q002 option b 'violates-qualifier', option d 'wrong-configuration'), but no Why-not line in 5-quiz.md names the type, and 1-fast.md never lists the types (only the keyword-bait trap). The chapter's stated job is to teach how questions are built, including distractor types; the practice never makes her use them. Print the type in each Why-not line (for example 'Type 1, loses on the qualifier') and list the six types in the fast file.
findings.resolution: fix-01: deferred to the orchestrator. Printing distractor_type in each Why-not line is a change to the sync generator, whose format TOOLS-items.md 6.2 fixes. Listing the six types in 1-fast would push sections that are already over their word budgets (W201) further over.

findings.quote: 5. Between the gateway endpoint and the interface endpoint the difference is who can use the endpoint. My first idea breaks because gateway endpoints do not allow access from on-premises networks
findings.evidence: The chapter's questions are meant to teach reading the stem, not AWS facts (registry/orchestrator note for 01). Q1/Q2 (gateway vs interface endpoint pricing and on-premises reach), Q9 (network ACL rule order, security-group references) and Q10 (SCP scope) are decided by service facts that chapter 01 never teaches; on her study route she meets this chapter before IAM and VPC. She can follow the think-aloud but cannot reproduce it on an unseen question, so the items test recall of later chapters rather than qualifier spotting. Either add one sentence of the needed fact before each worked example, or swap the deciding fact for one that the stem itself states (as q002/q006 do: the stem says 'acceptable' or 'must continue').
findings.resolution: fix-01: the question slots and their deciding facts are fixed in brief.json, which the orchestrator owns (TOOLS-rules R4). Swapping the deciding fact changes which answer is correct and would reset verification. Each of these items already states its deciding fact, with a fact link, in Why, Why not and Twin. The worked steps teach the reading method: qualifier first, then requirements.

findings.section: The nine word groups / Optimisation qualifiers
findings.quote: ### Optimisation qualifiers (1 min)
findings.evidence: RULINGS 2026-10-04: 'Spelling: American English everywhere (data center, analyze, optimize)'. 'Optimisation' is British. It comes from the group title in data/exam-english.json (id qualifiers) and propagates to the generated exam-english.md heading and to the Review links in 5-quiz.md (anchor #optimisation-qualifiers-1-min, Questions 1 and 2). Fix the data title to 'Optimization qualifiers', re-sync, and update the anchors.
findings.resolution: fix-01: deferred to the orchestrator. brief.json already notes this choice: the heading, its section id 'optimisation-qualifiers', two question sections and the data title must change together. brief.json belongs to the orchestrator (R4), and a rename only in the hand file fails L905.

findings.section: The nine word groups / Data and time
findings.quote: | transactional | several changes succeed together or fail together | a relational database, unless the stem also asks for another model |
findings.evidence: Hard rule 1 (a 'points to X' signal is a behavior claim) and no fact in the canon supports that 'transactional' signals a relational database. Amazon DynamoDB supports transactions, and SAA stems that say 'transactional' with key-value access or serverless scale expect DynamoDB. Rewrite the signal as 'check which database the options offer; both relational engines and some NoSQL services support transactions' or ground it in a fact.
findings.resolution: fix-01: same as claims-007; the signal is now 'a database with ACID transactions: a relational engine, or Amazon DynamoDB transactions'.

findings.quote: A gateway endpoint connects to Amazon S3 and DynamoDB, not to a partner API on the internet, so the calls do not arrive.
findings.evidence: An implicit 'only' claim without a fact link (RULINGS hard rule 1). The verified fact exists and is already in sources.md: vpc-gateway-endpoint-s3-dynamodb-no-privatelink, quote "Gateway VPC endpoints provide reliable connectivity to Amazon S3 and DynamoDB without requiring an internet gateway or a NAT device for your VPC." Link it. The Twin line of the same item ('it reaches Amazon S3 without a NAT device') can use the same fact.
findings.resolution: fix-01: the q005 why c and twin both link vpc-gateway-endpoint-s3-dynamodb-no-privatelink with its registered display (same as claims-014).

findings.quote: What is the MOST cost-effective solution that meets these requirements? / Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
findings.evidence: The ten items use only two qualifiers (MOST cost-effective: q004, q008, q002, q006; LEAST operational overhead: q003, q005, q007, q010, q011) and one item without a qualifier (q001). MOST secure, LEAST development effort, MOST operationally efficient and LOWEST latency, all taught in the qualifiers table, are never practised, although Secure is her weakest domain (READER.md, 45%). Swap one twin into a MOST secure stem.
findings.resolution: fix-01: deferred to the orchestrator. A MOST secure item needs a new or re-stemmed question, which changes the answer and needs a fresh verification. The qualifier mix of the slots is fixed in brief.json.

findings.section: Read the stem in this order
findings.quote: 1. **Read the ask.** Read the last sentence first, and find the capital word.
findings.evidence: The method assumes every ask has a capital qualifier, but q001 (5-quiz.md Question 3) asks 'What should a solutions architect do?' with none. The chapter never says what to do then (the requirements alone decide; there is usually one option that meets them all). One sentence in step 1 closes the gap.
findings.resolution: fix-01: step 1 now ends 'With no capital word, the requirements alone decide.'

findings.section: Read the stem in this order
findings.quote: Second: does it solve a different problem? Yes removes it.
findings.evidence: The figure (diagrams/src/how-the-exam-asks-option-ladder.json) has a rung 'Does it solve a different problem?' that the six numbered steps do not have, and Recap 1 asks for 'the six reading steps' only. Skimming the figure and the list gives two different procedures. Add the rung to step 4 ('Remove what breaks a requirement or solves a different problem').
findings.resolution: fix-01: step 4 and the Recap 1 answer now read 'Remove what breaks a requirement or solves a different problem'.

findings.quote: A **service control policy** (SCP) can do that. It [restricts permissions for IAM users and roles in member accounts](../facts/iam.md#iam-scp-applies-to-member-root-user)
findings.evidence: The fast file of a front chapter introduces SCP, member accounts and the member root user inside a trap bullet, with only an xref to chapter 04 (lint W601). The point of the trap (ensure vs detect) does not need the SCP; the service detail is a leap for the 10-minute route. Keep the example in q011 and cut the SCP sentences here, or move them to a Go deeper block.
findings.resolution: fix-01: the brief's truth for trap detect-meets-ensure names the SCP and its fact iam-scp-applies-to-member-root-user, so the example stays. It is now tied to 'the practice question', and the trap leads with the reading point (a stem that says 'no one can' asks for a control that stops the action).

findings.quote: Patching shows the difference. ... The guide's phrase for decouple is [decoupling workloads so that components can scale independently]
findings.evidence: The paragraph sets up the twin 'fully managed against provision', but patching illustrates managed vs self-managed, not provision vs on-demand, and the next sentence jumps to decoupling with no link to either. Split: one sentence that shows the provision side (you size and pay in advance), and move the decouple quote to the table intro or cut it.
findings.resolution: fix-01: the provision side now says 'you choose and size capacity in advance, and you pay for that capacity'; the patching paragraph is introduced as what fully managed takes away; the decouple quote is its own short paragraph before the table ('The table also holds decouple').

findings.quote: | manages its own keys | the company, not AWS, controls the encryption keys | customer managed keys; if the stem says the keys stay outside AWS, look at the options that support that |
findings.evidence: Rule: a signal must say what to look for. 'Look at the options that support that' gives her nothing to recognize in an option. Name the option shape (for example imported key material or an external key store), grounded in a KMS fact, or cut the second half.
findings.resolution: fix-01: second half cut; the signal is now 'customer managed keys in a key service; check who must control rotation'.

findings.quote: It works, but one shared role serves every instance, because a role change [propagates to all of them](../facts/iam.md#iam-ec2-role-credentials-rotate-automatically); extra roles add work.
findings.evidence: The 'because' does not explain the cause: one role can serve many instances because an instance profile can hold the same role on every instance; propagation is a benefit of sharing, not the reason it is possible. Rewrite as 'one shared role serves every instance, and a change to it propagates to all of them; separate roles multiply the work'.
findings.resolution: fix-01: rewritten as suggested: 'It works, but one shared role serves every instance, and a change to that role [propagates to all of them]; separate roles multiply the work.'

findings.quote: ## Optimisation qualifiers ... (90 rows, identical to the tables in 2-deep.md)
findings.evidence: exam-english.md repeats the nine tables of 2-deep.md row for row; the only difference is the absence of the hand text. data/exam-english.json holds an example stem sentence for every word (field 'stem', for example 'The clickstream data must be available for analysis in near real-time.') that the reader sees nowhere. For a second-language reader an example sentence per word teaches more than a duplicate table: show the stem line in exam-english.md (a fourth column or a line under each table).
findings.resolution: fix-01: deferred to the orchestrator. exam-english.md is generated by sync from data/exam-english.json, so showing the stem sentence is a generator change under the TOOLS contract.

findings.quote: | Where | Online or at a test center, through [Pearson VUE](../facts/exam.md#exam-testing-options) |
findings.evidence: The registry note for 01 names the ten official sample questions as a format reference (saved as _build/work/01-how-the-exam-asks/sample-questions.pdf), but no chapter file mentions them or tells her where AWS publishes them. One line with the link (no copied content) in the logistics table or the method section would let her see the real format once.
findings.resolution: fix-01: deferred. The registry note for 01 says the sample-questions PDF is not recorded (binary, on d1.awsstatic.com), and no fact or source carries its URL. A link needs the URL recorded first (registry or corpus) by the orchestrator.
